source_review.notes: Checked current official Amazon S3 consistency and ListObjectsV2 documentation; Google Cloud Storage consistency, objects-list, metadata, and caching documentation; Azure List Blobs, geo-redundancy, and concurrency documentation; and the original Herlihy-Wing linearizability paper. All ten URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date. Sources support the scoped strong-listing, pagination, metadata-revision, cache, secondary-index, primary/secondary replication, and real-time-history claims.

evidence: Reviewed namespace revision mapping, exact object and metadata identities, immutable listing query, page token, scan multiset, authoritative and derived sets, page capacity, scan duration, mutation rate, watermark, and lag notation.
Checked key equality is never substituted for version equality and a continuation token is not treated as a key or revision.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Provider generations, versions, metagenerations, validators, timestamps, cursors, and stream watermarks remain distinct.

evidence: Executed live-list-pagination with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced pages (a,c), (d,f), and (g), scan (a,c,d,f,g), initial (a,c,e,g), and final (a,b,c,d,f,g).
Reproduced missing final key b, newly observed keys d and f, and false snapshot equality.
Recomputed 2.4 billion keys divided by a 1,000-item maximum as a quiet-set lower bound of 2,400,000 requests.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The live-pagination fixture is a generic model, not a claim about an undocumented provider implementation.

evidence: Checked the request lower bound ceil(K/P) and mutation-exposure approximation lambda times T with their stated assumptions.
Verified reconciliation sets A-D and D-A distinguish missing and extra identities while version mismatch remains a separate relation.
Traced per-request linearization versus a scan-wide fixed namespace revision and confirmed one does not imply the other.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Mutation exposure is explicitly not presented as an exact omission or duplication count.

evidence: Reviewed empty/single/full/short pages, empty pages with a next token, repeated/expired/invalid tokens, stable and changed queries, lexical and unordered namespaces, and page-size-one behavior.

Reviewed inserts and deletes before/after cursors, same-key replacement, metadata-only update, ambiguous writes, permission changes, throttling, crash between output/checkpoint, and overlapping scan partitions.
Reviewed stale caches, asynchronous replicas, delayed tag indexes, inventory lag, stream retention gaps, delete markers, versions, snapshots, soft deletes, uncommitted state, and unsafe cleanup.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Primary namespace, cache, replica, event, inventory, and secondary-index surfaces are tested separately.

evidence: Traced exact provider/resource/endpoint/query/API/auth context through scan identity and continuation checkpoints.
Checked page output and next cursor are atomic or replay-safe, rows bind exact versions, partitions are disjoint, and destructive actions revalidate current versions and policy.
Checked snapshot, immutable-manifest, and live-scan-plus-change-capture protocols each state their distinct completion proof.
invariant_checking.notes: A successful iterator loop is never used as proof of snapshot membership or safe deletion.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step listing audit from contract scoping through desired result, real-time history, pagination, identity, protocol choice, checkpointing, derived surfaces, conditional mutation, and lag measurement.
Checked the fixture is a counterexample to scan-wide snapshot inference: the emitted set includes later insertions, misses another later insertion, and omits an initial deletion.

Reviewed baseline-plus-change-stream proof requirements: pre-scan watermark, replay coverage, exact version identity, idempotent application, terminal watermark, retention, and periodic reconciliation.
proof_review.notes: Counts, quiet tests, LIST absence, and key equality are rejected as insufficient proof where exact membership or identity matters.

evidence: Audited uses of strong, linearizable, snapshot, exact, complete, authoritative, current, safe, atomic, idempotent, converged, and bounded.
Confirmed provider claims are scoped to named endpoints and dated official documentation and the model explicitly disclaims undocumented provider behavior.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Per-request and scan-wide claims are consistently separated.

evidence: Reviewed page capacity, request count, duration, mutation rate, cache freshness, event/index/replica lag, inventory age, throttling, retry, and scan restart measurements.
Confirmed no universal provider latency, token lifetime, page fill, index lag, replica lag, cache purge time, regulatory approval, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production evidence requires exact product/API version, endpoint, resource type, workload, concurrency history, authorization, and observation path.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed consistency vocabulary, operation histories, per-request versus scan semantics, opaque pagination, ordering, object/metadata identity, indexes, caches, replicas, manifests, snapshots, change capture, reconciliation, restart, cost, cleanup, and tests as one coherent discovery model.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed durable scan records, exact query/token scope, idempotent page persistence, version-specific processing, immutable manifests, stream retention, reconciliation, cache/replica/index watermarks, conditional deletion, rate limits, and canaries. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from consistency vocabulary and counterexample through production protocols and governance; ten examples and five complete answers cover live pagination, billion-key checkpointing, LIST/HEAD races, stream-backed catalogs, and regulated deletion.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external distributed-systems researcher, cloud-provider representative, storage-client maintainer, data catalog operator, security auditor, records/privacy/legal specialist, research-ethics authority, or certification review is claimed.
